This removes hermes\' bundled desktop-automation tool (cua-driver). It is only used in that kind of session, and it won\'t come back on its own — run hermes pm install once in the terminal to get it back (needs network, takes a while).
Browser tools (agent-browser / chromium) are not removed — hermes needs them to open web pages, so they stay.

ffmpeg isn\'t included either: it\'s a required package for hermes, and removing it makes hermes report \"install out of sync\" on every start (it doesn\'t accept the copy bundled with the system layer).

When the process is killed, the system records why (out of memory / resource limit exceeded / vendor background cleanup / crash / not responding). It\'s collected here on the next launch. Heartbeats are logged every 10 minutes, and the last one shows the state right before it died (memory level, whether the foreground service was running, which page you were on). Export it and send it to the author for analysis.

Zhengdao needs to read and write your files, and to notify you when a cleanup finishes. It needs the permissions below. You can grant them one by one, or set them up later (Settings → Permissions, any time).

With this on, agents can reach a wider range of storage. Basic /sdcard read/write works without it; this device doesn\'t offer the switch for Zhengdao, so leaving it off is normal and costs you nothing.
Silent notes like \"cleaned up after install\" use notifications. Without the permission the system discards them, but no feature is affected.

Bound to %1$s only (loopback). That means this port is reachable only from the phone itself — not from the internet, not from other devices on your network, and not from other apps on this phone.

How to use it (for terminal agents)

In the terminal, note the passphrase first: export BRIDGE_TOKEN=<the string you just copied>. After that your agent can drive the browser tab over loopback, e.g.:
curl -s -u browser:$BRIDGE_TOKEN http://127.0.0.1:14080/bridge/v1/status
Commands: status / snapshot / navigate / click / type / scroll / newTab / activeTab / closeTab / screenshot / execJS.
Note: an agent can do a lot on a page (including typing into password fields), but it cannot touch app-private data, change browser security settings, or switch privacy redaction off.

Hidden by default: Baopu unlocks it when needed (this session only)

Only core tools show by default; low-frequency groups unlock on demand. "Hidden" is not "disabled" — the model simply never sees them; it calls capabilities to open a group (a new session goes back to default). The switch on the right is a GROUP switch: once a group is off, capabilities cannot unlock it either (your switch wins). Each tool inside keeps its own switch too — the two tiers coexist and neither overrides the other.
Groups start collapsed: tap a group name to expand or collapse. While collapsed the group keeps a standing summary line of what is switched off - tools you turned off never hide behind the fold.

Look and unlock: lists every tool group with a one-line summary and who is default-visible / unlocked / switched off by you, then unlocks groups for this session. It only changes "which tools the model can see this round" and touches no files, so no confirmation card. A group you switched off stays locked — and it will say so honestly.

Sends one workspace file to the XuanLan "local preview" tab to **display only**: HTML renders, anything else shows as source, with a source/render toggle and copy. The tab is offline by default (every in-page http/https request is intercepted with an empty response) and runs no scripts by default; with the script sandbox on it still runs only inside that tab and still cannot reach the network. It never executes your program, never touches a terminal or rootfs, and rejects paths outside the workspace. Writes no files, so no confirmation card.

Edit images (a confirmation card pops up before each run): resize to a max edge, crop by rectangle, convert to png/jpg/webp, extract the dominant palette (text only), or generate 48/72/96/144/192 square icon PNGs. The original is never overwritten — output goes to <name>-<action>.<ext> and an existing target is refused.

Delete one file in the workspace (a confirmation card pops up before each run): by default it is **moved to the recycle bin** (workspace/.回收站/<stamp>-<name>), so it can be moved back; only with \"permanent\" ticked is it unrecoverable. Files only — directories are always refused; the backup area .baopu-bak/, the recycle bin itself and 资料库/原始/ are off limits.
